claim: The healthy cornea has no blood vessels; it is nourished by oxygen dissolved in tears diffusing through its layers (oxygen comes from the air)
Corneal neovascularization (blood vessel ingrowth) is caused by deprivation of oxygen from the air - the risk raised by hypoxic conditions such as overnight contact lens wear

source URL: ~90% of infectious (microbial) keratitis cases are bacterial; Pseudomonas aeruginosa is responsible for ~40% of those bacterial cases

claim: P. aeruginosa produces enzymes that can digest the cornea; infectious keratitis can progress rapidly (overnight-wear and tap-water exposure are documented risk practices)
A corneal ulcer involves loss of epithelial tissue with stromal involvement; complications include corneal scarring
source URL: and severe cases can need corneal transplant

claim: Acanthamoeba keratitis is rare (~100 US cases/yr) but nearly always associated with soft contact lens use; 89% of infected patients in a 20-yr Austrian study were lens wearers and 19% required a corneal transplant; amoebae can come from tap water
Storing/rinsing lenses in tap water is a documented risk practice (never let lenses touch tap water)
